name: Cerulean Cataract

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Slit-Lamp Diagnostic Criteria for Cerulean Cataract

criteria.description: Presence of multiple small, blue-white opacities scattered in the lens cortex
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Mild to moderate visual impairment related to lens opacities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic blue-white cortical opacities in both lenses with or without positive family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by slit-lamp examination; genetic testing may confirm mutations in CRYBB2 or other crystallin genes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple small blue-white cortical lens opacities
searchTerms: multiple small white-blue spots on lens cortex
small cloudy spots in lens outer layer
lens changes in both eyes equally

common.symptomName: Mild to moderate decrease in visual acuity
searchTerms: some loss of sharpness in sight
irregular lens shape causing blurred vision
distorted vision due to lens shape
increased glare or light scatter in eye
vision affected by intraocular light scatter
early cataract development before old age
cloudy membrane behind lens after surgery

imaging: Slit-lamp biomicroscopy revealing multiple blue-white cortical opacities
Anterior segment optical coherence tomography (AS-OCT) showing lens opacity distribution
genetic: Mutations in CRYBB2 gene associated with autosomal dominant inheritance
other: Family pedigree analysis consistent with autosomal dominant transmission

distinguishingFeatures: Opacity localized to Y-sutures of the lens
Usually non-progressive and less likely to cause visual impairment
Opacity confined to a specific lamella of the lens
Often associated with perinatal insults or metabolic disorders
Similar blue-white opacities but typically smaller and less numerous
May be sporadic rather than familial

redFlags: Rapid progression of lens opacity causing sudden vision loss
Unilateral lens opacity with inflammation suggesting secondary causes
Signs of secondary glaucoma or lens-induced uveitis
references: Shiels A, Hejtmancik JF. Crystallins and cataractogenesis. Prog Mol Biol Transl Sci. 2015;134:259-275.
Francis PJ, Berry V, Bhattacharya SS. Molecular genetics of cataract. Eye (Lond). 2000;14 ( Pt 3B): 390-396.
